newsitem.title: USA: Bell may post "marginal" Q1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Bell may post "marginal" Q1 loss.

text.p: Bell Industries Inc on Monday said it may post a "marginal" net loss for the first quarter.

In a statement, the company said transition costs related to the integration of recently acquired Milgray Electronics and reduced shipments of electronic components, including memory products, are expected to result in a 20 percent to 30 percent decline in operating income, before, special items, compared to the pro forma combined operating income for the first quarter of last year.

In addition, Bell said it expects to record a special before-tax charge ranging between $4 million and $6 million for costs associated with the integration of Milgray, which may result in a marginal net loss for the quarter.
The special charge includes provisions for employee severance, lease commitments, and costs related to supplier terminations.

Bell will also record an extraordinary charge of $675,000, net of tax, as a result of the early retirement of Bell's 9.70 percent Senior Notes, which were replaced under Bell's now credit agreement with a banking syndicate.

On a pro forma basis, for the quarter ended March 31, 1996, Bell and Milgray combined sales were approximately $214 million, operating income, was $12 million, and net income was $3.7 million, or $0.49 per share.

Bell said its consolidated sales for the first quarter of 1997 are expected to be slightly higher, when compared to the pro forma revenues of Bell and Milgray combined in 1996. On a combined basis, sales of electronic components are below last year as a result of the transition to the new Samsung distribution franchise from National Semiconductor Corp and reduced shipments of memory products.
The company said trends affecting the first quarter operating results are expected to continue through the second quarter.
